instructions: Read the complete lesson in order without assuming earlier knowledge beyond what it explicitly recalls. Record concrete gaps with the passage and repair.
Can a student explain the question, why it matters, their final product and how the lesson will help before the first task?
Does each person, document, label and term have a meaning before the first instruction that uses it?
Does the worked example model decisions and why, instead of presenting only a polished answer or a list of amounts?
Do calculations match the unchanged records and explain units, duration, exclusions and the decision they inform?
Are section transitions purposeful, with no duplicate instructions, unexplained reset or hidden essential teaching?
Does supported practice invite an attempt before intentional feedback/model support? Does a new person get their own facts and conditions?
Do independent prompts, field labels, model content and signoff requirements ask for the same product? Are multiple evidence-supported answers handled fairly?
Do retained media and sources have an explicit purpose and usable text equivalents, with their original limits preserved?
Does the rendered lesson exactly match the manuscript, retain the approved course style and support native vocabulary keyboard use?
Compare all task controls, IDs, versions, media, history and completion requirements to the frozen original. Structural counts are compatibility evidence, not proof of teaching quality.
Keep teacher acceptance, source review, local technical checks, canonical integration and release proof as separate statuses.
